doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: To the US and the Caribbean with Carmen and Rolando
title: Chicago snow, La Conga and the dancers' act
summary: After the Latin Quarter in Chicago they went to La Conga with Machito, Pupi Campo and Miguelito Valdes; he describes the dance repertoire and his fifteen-minute drum solo.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When we ended the contract in the Havana Madrid, we went to Chicago. The pair of dancers and I, to the Latin Quarter of Chicago. By the way I had never seen snow until we got to Chicago. And when we got to Chicago there was a snowstorm and I said to the pair of dancers, "Look sperm is falling from the sky." (Laughs.) After we finished up there in the Latin Quarter of Chicago, we came to the Cabaret La Conga in New York. The orchestras of Machito and Pupi Campo were there. And the star of the show was Miguelito Valdés.
Now what was the dance repertoire of Carmen and Rolando composed of?
Well, in three parts: first a bolero, then a rumba, and then . . . yes those two. First, a very slow bolero and then the rumba. That was their repertoire. Well I say three because then
came my solo – me alone with the conga and the quinto.
And more or less how much time?
Did the entire show last, or our part?
Oh my part? It lasted like, I would say about fifteen minutes.
So you went at it there alone. . .
Alone. Corporan:. . . on drums for fifteen minutes alternating between bongo and?
Everything . . . it was something to see . . . (Laughs) All of the Afro-Cuban rhythms.

So then I accompanied them. But I opened the show and I would stay on to accompany them. When they finished, Miguelito Valdés then closed the show. That was at the Cabaret La Conga in 1946. After there we went to Puerto Rico. From Puerto Rico, we went to . .
